newsitem.title: LEBANON: Israeli jets attack guerrillas in south Lebanon.
newsitem.headline: Israeli jets attack guerrillas in south Lebanon.

text.p: Israeli jets rocketed suspected guerrilla targets in south Lebanon hills on Saturday hours after an Israeli-backed militia patrol was ambushed, security sources said.

They said the planes fired four rockets into Louwaizeh hills in Iqlim al-Toufah, a rugged ridge used by pro-Iranian Hizbollah (Party of God) guerrillas to attack Israeli troops and their militia allies occupying a south Lebanon border zone.
The was no immediate report of casualties in the air attack, which came hours after guerrillas ambushed a patrol of the Israeli-backed South Lebanon Army (SLA) militia in Markaba in the border zone.
No one was hurt in the ambush, SLA sources said.
Saturday's air raid was the fifth on Lebanon in little over two weeks.

On Wednesday an Israeli helicopter rocketed a Hizbollah target in Iqlim al-Toufah after the Moslem fighters wounded two Israeli soldiers in a mortar bomb attack against an Israeli outpost in the border strip.

No group immediately claimed responsibility for the attack against the SLA patrol but Hizbollah and other guerrillas wage attacks against Israeli and SLA forces in a bid to drive them out from the south Lebanon zone.

The Syrian-backed Amal Movement said in a statement that its guerrillas fired mortar bombs, anti-tank rockets and machineguns at an Israeli post at Qasseer and an SLA post at Alman to the northeast of Markaba and just inside the zone.
There was no immediate independent confirmation of the report.

Some 1,000 Israeli troops and the 3,000-strong SLA hold the zone stretching along the border from Mount Hermon in the east to the Mediterranean in the west since 1985 to ward off cross-frontier guerrilla raids on northern Israel.
